# Memory and workspace lifetime
There is no idle TTL. Code-query caches have an independent estimated admission budget of 64 MiB per project. KNOWLEDGE_RAIL_WORKSPACE_STATE_CAP sets the workspace LRU cap. This is not a limit on heap or RSS. External changes are checked on the next query.

# Markdown Python example
```python
# internalneedle preserves the code comment
print(1)
```
## Outside
ordinary text

# Relative module references
Relative import paths resolve explicit TypeScript extensions. Runtime .js imports can resolve .ts or .tsx sources only when unambiguous. Package imports and configured aliases resolve supported explicit local declarations; dynamic or undeclared configurations remain unresolved. Different directories never share a basename-only import edge.

# Checkpoint recovery
A checkpoint builder mismatch triggers snapshot_builder_mismatch. Canonical Markdown rebuilds persisted passages after a builder upgrade. Corrupt derived checkpoints are discarded and rebuilt from canonical evidence.

# Workspace LRU
Workspace LRU retains five workspaces by default. Registration and access determine eviction order independently of system clock timestamps. Releasing the final binding evicts disposable workspace state.

# Incremental updates
removeCheckpointRecord derives the changed page terms. It removes only those postings and drops terms without documents. Journal replay preserves token counts.

# File reconciliation
File reconciliation bounds concurrency to 64 operations. Scan errors propagate. Notifications received during reconciliation remain dirty for the next query.

# Historical cache decision
Obsolete decision, superseded: cache expiry uses TTL 60 seconds. This historical claim contradicts the current cache policy [[concepts/cache]].

# Module A
Module in directory alpha handles invoices; its identifier is alpha/Module.ts.

# Module B
Module in directory beta handles refunds; its identifier is beta/Module.ts.

# Python adapter limits
Python adapter records module strings from import and from clauses. Module resolution is a heuristic, not a Python interpreter. Dynamic imports are not guaranteed.
